title: Partial region egress saturation retrospective + runbook appendix
content:
Summary:

On 2025-02-10 between ~02:23 and 03:14 UTC we observed degraded request completion rates for customer-facing endpoints from the us-west-2 region. Root impact: a subset of egress paths out of the region experienced sustained saturation which triggered TCP retransmit storms and application-level retries. This produced an amplification effect: clients retried -> more egress -> further saturation -> higher latency and 5xx surface.

Scope / Impact:
- Affected surface: hosted API endpoints for ~15% of traffic originating from US-West clients (routing weight estimate).
- Observed symptoms: high tail latency for text-generation endpoints, increased 502/504s from edge proxies, KV cache miss spikes, and a rise in per-request token cost from retries.
- Customer visible: brief API errors and timeouts, elevated response times for ~50 minutes before mitigation stabilized.

Timeline (UTC):
- 02:22: first alert from synthetic canaries (p95 latency > 2x baseline).
- 02:23: on-call SRE (Marco) acknowledges; initial dashboard shows egress interface TX errors and queue growth on region-egress-02.
- 02:30: automated circuit-breaker for heavy model routes triggered in us-west-2 (reduced concurrency targets).
- 02:34: retries increase from clients; routing controller reports backlog for regional proxy pool.
- 02:42: team decides to shift 40% of us-west-2 weight to us-west-1 warm standby (manual weighted-routing change).
- 02:55: KV cache preseed had partial miss due to traffic shift; short-lived quality regressions for a subset of requests.
- 03:05: egress metrics show downward trend; 03:14: p95 latency returned below threshold, alerts auto-resolved.

Root cause (current hypothesis):
- Primary trigger: transient bandwidth congestion on one of the ISP egress links serving us-west-2, likely due to an unrelated external peering flap at the provider (evidence: interface-level TX drops, provider TO records pending).
- Secondary contributors: aggressive client retry policies + lack of early request shedding at the edge for certain model-heavy routes. Also, regional autoscaling was slow to add proxy capacity because the saturation was at network egress, not CPU/GPU, so autoscaler did not react.
- No evidence of software bug in model runtime itself; errors aligned with network-level counters.

Mitigations executed (chronological):
1) Circuit-breaker activation on heavy routes (02:30) — reduced per-connection concurrency to slow token emission and client retry amplification.
2) Manual weighted routing shift (02:42) — moved 40% traffic from us-west-2 -> us-west-1 (warm standby pool).
3) Temporary client-facing retry window increase: allowed longer backoff in proxy to reduce immediate replays (02:47).
4) Egress interface soft-disable for the most noisy peering pair and re-route via alternate provider (coordinated with cloud provider; 02:58).

What worked:
- Weighted routing change was effective and fast (manual change took ~2 min to apply across routing controllers).
- Circuit-breaker reduced instantaneous QPS and limited retry amplification.
- Observability (edge metrics + interface counters) had sufficient fidelity to detect TX errors quickly.

What didn't work / surprises:
- Autoscaler did not help because it looks at host CPU/GPU usage; it has no signal for network egress saturation. Need an egress saturation detector to trigger horizontal proxy scaling or traffic shaping.
- KV cache preseed assumptions failed for the traffic shifted to standby — we got more cache misses than anticipated, causing transient quality variance.
- Runbook steps for peering provider coordination were incomplete; contacting provider took longer than expected due to non-standard escalation path.

Immediate runbook changes (appendixed below)
- Add an "Egress-saturation checklist" to oncall runbook with clear thresholds and single-command traffic shift script.
- Add a quick toggle to disable aggressive client retry headers at the edge (edge-config mutation endpoint) for a region.
- Document provider escalation contacts and templates in the SRE shared-drive.

Diagnostics & useful queries (copy/paste):
- PromQL: sum(rate(egress_tx_errors_total{region="us-west-2"}[1m])) by (peer)
- PromQL: sum(rate(proxy_request_duration_seconds_bucket{region="us-west-2"}[1m])) by (le)
- Fleet check: kubectl -n infra get pods -l role=regional-proxy -o wide --context=us-west-2
- Edge probe: curl -v -H 'X-Debug: routing' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=gpt-j-test
- Cache health: curl https://cache-admin.us-west-2.internal/metrics | grep kv_cache_hit_rate

Runbook appendix (commands, thresholds, and play actions):
- Trigger thresholds:
  - If egress_tx_errors_total rate > 5/min for >3 minutes -> escalate to oncall lead and consider weighted shift.
  - If p99 latency > 2x baseline AND 5xx rate > 1% -> enable circuit-breaker on heavy routes.

- Quick-weighted-shift (single command):
  - ./routingctl set-weight --region us-west-2 --target us-west-1 --percent 40 --reason "egress_saturation"
  - Verify: ./routingctl get-weights --region us-west-2
  - Rollback: ./routingctl set-weight --region us-west-2 --target us-west-1 --percent 0 --reason "rollback"

- Edge retry policy toggle:
  - API: POST https://edge-config.redwood/api/v1/toggles/retry-window
  - body: {"region":"us-west-2","backoff_multiplier":2.5}
  - Verify response header X-Edge-Retry-Policy in synthetic probes.

- Provider escalation template (email/portal):
  - Subject: "Urgent: egress interface errors observed for us-west-2 (instance: region-egress-02)"
  - Body: include time window, counters (TX errors), backbone IDs, request traces, and ask for immediate path reroute or rate limiting on offending upstream. Attach pcap if requested.

Post-incident action items (owners & ETA):
- Add egress saturation metric -> autoscaler signal (Priyanka) — ETA 2025-03-15.
- Implement preseed warm-standby KV cache hook on weight change (Lena) — ETA 2025-03-01 (high priority).
- Add provider escalation runbook & secure contact list (Devon) — ETA 2025-02-28 (done).
- Add tests to routing controller to validate weight change roll-forward/rollback under partial-cache conditions (Marco) — ETA 2025-03-10.

Longer-term ideas / R&D signals:
- Prototype a network-aware autoscaler that consumes egress link metrics and can spin up regional-proxy pods in the warm-standby region automatically when egress saturation detected.
- Experiment with token pacing at the edge (gradual emit instead of bursts) to avoid spiky egress from single requests.
- Investigate per-peer shaping in the egress layer to minimize blast radius of a noisy upstream.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Confirm whether provider reported maintenance or BGP flap for the time window; contact ticket tracked in linked_artifacts.
- Evaluate if client SDKs should include jittered exponential backoff by default for heavy-model calls.
- Revisit our default DNS TTL for routing weights — shorter TTLs allow faster shifts but increase DNS query load.

Appendix: quick checklist for future on-call shifts
1) Verify egress counters and identify which peer(s) show TX errors.
2) Reduce per-route concurrency via circuit-breaker for the heaviest model routes.
3) Execute weighted routing shift (start with 25% -> 50% depending on impact).
4) Preseed KV cache on target region if possible; otherwise expect a short quality delta and notify product owners.
5) Coordinate with provider if interface errors persist after routing change.
6) Reassess and rollback weights gradually after egress stabilizes for 20+ minutes.

Appendix: quick links
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-4821
- Routing controller PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412
- Cache preseed design doc: CONFLUENCE-REPO-820

End of doc.

(Informal notes: this one felt like a classic "egress-layer" incident rather than application compute; adding network signals to autoscaler should reduce cognitive load for next oncall.)
